evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Bmp4−/E93G compound mutants were recovered at the predicted Mendelian frequency through E14.5.

claim: At E13.5–14.5, all Bmp4−/E93G mutants were slightly runted relative to littermates.

claim: All Bmp4−/E93G mutants had defects in ventral body wall closure in which the liver was partially or fully externalized at E13.5–14.5.
source: At E13.5–14.5, all Bmp4−/E93G mutants were slightly runted relative to littermates and had defects in ventral body wall closure in which the liver was partially or fully externalized (n = 16/16) (Figure 4A–G).
evidence: This is supported by visual observation shown in Figure 4A–G.

claim: Most Bmp4−/E93G embryos had small or absent eyes at E13.5–14.5.

claim: Hearts dissected from Bmp4−/E93G mutants at E14.5 revealed highly trabeculated ventricular walls that failed to undergo compaction.

claim: Hearts dissected from Bmp4−/E93G mutants at E14.5 revealed ventricular septal defects.
source: Histological examination of hearts dissected from Bmp4−/E93G mutants at E14.5 revealed highly trabeculated ventricular walls that failed to undergo compaction (3/3) and ventricular septal defects (2/3) (VSDs) (Figure 4I) that were never observed in wild type embryos (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 4I.

claim: A similar spectrum of abnormalities including small or absent eyes, failure to close the ventral body wall and VSDs have previously been reported in mice with reduced dosage of Bmp4.

evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bmp4S91C/E93G female compound heterozygotes are underrepresented at weaning.

claim: Bmp4S91C/E93G mice appeared grossly normal at weaning.

claim: Bmp4S91C/E93G mice weighed slightly, but not significantly, less than littermates at weaning.
source: Bmp4S91C/E93G mice appeared grossly normal at weaning, although they weighed slightly, but not significantly, less than littermates (Figure 5).

claim: The late lethality of female Bmp4S91C/E93G compound heterozygotes and Bmp4E93G homozygotes contrasts with the early (E11) lethality of Bmp4S91C homozygotes.

evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of phenotypes across different genotypes.

claim: Loss of FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain fully accounts for the late lethality of Bmp4E93G/E93G and Bmp4S91C/E93G mutants.

evidence: This is speculation based on the differential severity of phenotypes.

claim: The p.S91C mutation may cause additional, FAM20C-independent defects in BMP4 function when encoded on both alleles of Bmp4.
source: These results raise the possibility that loss of FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain fully accounts for the late lethality of Bmp4E93G/E93G and Bmp4S91C/E93G mutants whereas the p.S91C mutation may cause additional, FAM20C-independent defects in BMP4 function when encoded on both alleles of Bmp4.
evidence: This is speculation based on the differential severity of phenotypes.

claim: Levels of pSMAD1 were significantly lower in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4S91C homozygotes compared to wild type controls.
source: Levels of BMP4 precursor protein were significantly higher, and levels of pSMAD1 and of cleaved BMP4 ligand were significantly lower in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4S91C homozygotes compared to wild type controls (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: Levels of cleaved BMP4 ligand were significantly lower in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4S91C homozygotes compared to wild type controls.
source: Levels of BMP4 precursor protein were significantly higher, and levels of pSMAD1 and of cleaved BMP4 ligand were significantly lower in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4S91C homozygotes compared to wild type controls (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: No significant differences in levels of pSMAD1, BMP4 precursor or BMP4 ligand were observed in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4E93G mutants compared to wild type controls.
source: No significant differences in levels of pSMAD1, BMP4 precursor or BMP4 ligand were observed in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4E93G mutants compared to wild type controls (Figure 6E–H), or in wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags compared to untagged controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6E–H.

claim: No significant differences in levels of pSMAD1, BMP4 precursor or BMP4 ligand were observed in wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags compared to untagged controls.
source: No significant differences in levels of pSMAD1, BMP4 precursor or BMP4 ligand were observed in E10.5 lysates from Bmp4E93G mutants compared to wild type controls (Figure 6E–H), or in wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags compared to untagged controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: pSMAD1 levels were significantly reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygous E13.5 MEFs compared to wild type controls.
source: When we repeated this analysis in E13.5 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) isolated from wild type or mutant littermates, we found that pSMAD1 levels were significantly reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygotes (Figure 6I, J) and in Bmp4E93G homozygotes (Figure 6M, N) compared to wild type controls.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6I, J.

claim: pSMAD1 levels were significantly reduced in Bmp4E93G homozygous E13.5 MEFs compared to wild type controls.
source: When we repeated this analysis in E13.5 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) isolated from wild type or mutant littermates, we found that pSMAD1 levels were significantly reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygotes (Figure 6I, J) and in Bmp4E93G homozygotes (Figure 6M, N) compared to wild type controls.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6M, N.

claim: Levels of BMP4 precursor protein were increased in Bmp4S91C heterozygous E13.5 MEFs compared to wild type controls.
source: In addition, levels of BMP4 precursor protein were increased and levels of cleaved ligand were reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygotes (Figure 6I, K, L) and in Bmp4E93G heterozygotes or homozygotes (Figure 6M, O, P) compared to wild type controls.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6I, K, L.

claim: Levels of cleaved ligand were reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygous E13.5 MEFs compared to wild type controls.
source: In addition, levels of BMP4 precursor protein were increased and levels of cleaved ligand were reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygotes (Figure 6I, K, L) and in Bmp4E93G heterozygotes or homozygotes (Figure 6M, O, P) compared to wild type controls.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6I, K, L.

claim: Levels of BMP4 precursor protein were increased in Bmp4E93G heterozygous or homozygous E13.5 MEFs compared to wild type controls.
source: In addition, levels of BMP4 precursor protein were increased and levels of cleaved ligand were reduced in Bmp4S91C heterozygotes (Figure 6I, K, L) and in Bmp4E93G heterozygotes or homozygotes (Figure 6M, O, P) compared to wild type controls.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6M, O, P.

claim: In E13.5 MEFs, p.E93G and p.S91C mutations in the prodomain of BMP4 interfere with proteolytic maturation of BMP4, leading to accumulation of unprocessed precursor protein and reduced levels of cleaved ligand and BMP activity in vivo.
source: Thus, in E13.5 MEFs, p.E93G and p.S91C mutations in the prodomain of BMP4 interfere with proteolytic maturation of BMP4, leading to accumulation of unprocessed precursor protein and reduced levels of cleaved ligand and BMP activity in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunoblot data from MEFs.

claim: A second more slowly migrating BMP4 precursor band was observed in lysates from embryos heterozygous or homozygous for the S91C or E93G mutation.
source: Notably, in lysates from embryos heterozygous or homozygous for the S91C or E93G mutation, a second more slowly migrating BMP4 precursor band was observed (Figure 6A, E, arrow) in a subset of experiments.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6A, E.

claim: The more slowly migrating BMP4 precursor band was never present in lysates from wild type littermates or in lysates from wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags.
source: This band was never present in lysates from wild type littermates or in lysates from wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating that the shift in migration is not due to the presence of epitope tags.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The shift in migration of the BMP4 precursor band is not due to the presence of epitope tags.
source: This band was never present in lysates from wild type littermates or in lysates from wild type embryos carrying HA and Myc epitope tags (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating that the shift in migration is not due to the presence of epitope tags.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that tagged wild type protein migrates normally.

claim: The BMP4 precursor band in extracts of MEFs isolated from Bmp4S91C/+ embryos migrated more slowly than that in MEFs isolated from wild type littermates.
source: The BMP4 precursor band in extracts of MEFs isolated from Bmp4S91C/+ embryos also migrated more slowly than that in MEFs isolated from wild type littermates (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Treatment of proteins with calf intestinal phosphatase or deglycosylases did not normalize the migration of the mutant BMP4 precursor band.
source: Treatment of proteins isolated from embryos or MEFs with calf intestinal phosphatase or treatment with deglycosylases to remove O- or N-linked glycosylation did not normalize the migration of this band.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from enzyme treatment experiments.

claim: The retarded migration of the mutant BMP4 precursor is unlikely to reflect differences in glycosylation or phosphorylation of mutant precursor protein relative to wild type.
source: Thus, the retarded migration is unlikely to reflect differences in glycosylation or phosphorylation of mutant precursor protein relative to wild type.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of phosphatase and deglycosylase treatment.

claim: FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of FGF23 is required for furin-mediated cleavage.
source: FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of FGF23, like that of BMP4, is required for furin-mediated cleavage (Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Phosphorylation of FGF23 prevents O-glycosylation of a nearby residue, and O-glycosylation sterically blocks the furin cleavage site.
source: Mechanistically, phosphorylation of FGF23 prevents O-glycosylation of a nearby residue, and O-glycosylation sterically blocks the furin cleavage site (Tagliabracci et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Treatment with O-glycosidase and neuraminidase led to a more rapid migration of the BMP4 precursor protein.
source: Treatment with these deglycosylases led to a more rapid migration of the BMP4 precursor protein, indicating that BMP4 is O-glycosylated, but there was no difference in the migration of wild type or point mutation precursors in the presence or absence of deglycosylases (Figure 7A), suggesting that phosphorylation does not alter O-glycosylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: BMP4 is O-glycosylated.
source: Treatment with these deglycosylases led to a more rapid migration of the BMP4 precursor protein, indicating that BMP4 is O-glycosylated, but there was no difference in the migration of wild type or point mutation precursors in the presence or absence of deglycosylases (Figure 7A), suggesting that phosphorylation does not alter O-glycosylation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of O-glycosidase treatment.

claim: There was no difference in the migration of wild type or point mutation BMP4 precursors in the presence or absence of deglycosylases.
source: Treatment with these deglycosylases led to a more rapid migration of the BMP4 precursor protein, indicating that BMP4 is O-glycosylated, but there was no difference in the migration of wild type or point mutation precursors in the presence or absence of deglycosylases (Figure 7A), suggesting that phosphorylation does not alter O-glycosylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Phosphorylation does not alter O-glycosylation of BMP4.
source: Treatment with these deglycosylases led to a more rapid migration of the BMP4 precursor protein, indicating that BMP4 is O-glycosylated, but there was no difference in the migration of wild type or point mutation precursors in the presence or absence of deglycosylases (Figure 7A), suggesting that phosphorylation does not alter O-glycosylation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of differential effect of deglycosylase treatment on wild type versus mutant precursors.

claim: Endo H-sensitive and Endo H-resistant forms of wild type and mutant BMP4 precursors were detected in MEFs.
source: As shown in Figure 7B, Endo H-sensitive (asterisks) and Endo H-resistant/PNGase F-sensitive (arrowheads) forms of wild type and mutant precursors were detected in MEFs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: High mannose, Endo H-sensitive carbohydrates are retained at one or more glycosylation site(s) on BMP4 ligand homodimers even after BMP4 has folded, trafficked through the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and been cleaved.
source: We have previously shown that high mannose, Endo H-sensitive carbohydrates are retained at one or more glycosylation site(s) on BMP4 ligand homodimers even after BMP4 has folded, trafficked through the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and been cleaved (Degnin et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain is not required for folding or exit of the precursor protein from the ER.
source: Collectively, our findings are consistent with a model in which FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain is not required for folding or exit of the precursor protein from the ER, but is required for proprotein convertase recognition and/or for trafficking to post-TGN compartment(s) where BMP4 is cleaved (Tilak et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the glycosylation analysis and prior research.

claim: FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain is required for proprotein convertase recognition and/or for trafficking to post-TGN compartment(s) where BMP4 is cleaved.
source: Collectively, our findings are consistent with a model in which FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation of the BMP4 prodomain is not required for folding or exit of the precursor protein from the ER, but is required for proprotein convertase recognition and/or for trafficking to post-TGN compartment(s) where BMP4 is cleaved (Tilak et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and prior research.

claim: Bmp4S91C and Bmp4E93G are hypomorphic alleles.
source: Our findings demonstrate that Bmp4S91C and Bmp4E93G are hypomorphic alleles, both of which carry mutations predicted to prevent FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation, but that Bmp4S91C mutants have a more severe loss of function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotypic analysis of the mutant mice.

claim: Bmp4S91C mutants have a more severe loss of function than Bmp4E93G mutants.
source: Our findings demonstrate that Bmp4S91C and Bmp4E93G are hypomorphic alleles, both of which carry mutations predicted to prevent FAM20C-mediated phosphorylation, but that Bmp4S91C mutants have a more severe loss of function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotypic analysis showing earlier lethality and more severe defects in Bmp4S91C mutants.

claim: The p.S91C mutation leads to additional defects in protein function independent of those caused by loss of phosphorylation.
source: It is likely that the p.S91C mutation leads to additional defects in protein function independent of those caused by loss of phosphorylation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the differential severity of phenotypes.

claim: The additional defects caused by p.S91C are likely due to deleterious effects of introducing an ectopic cysteine residue into the precursor protein.
source: These are likely due to deleterious effects of introducing an ectopic cysteine residue into the precursor protein.
evidence: This is speculation based on knowledge of cysteine chemistry and protein structure.

claim: BMP4 folds into a cystine knot containing three stereotypical intramolecular disulfide bonds that stabilize ligand monomers and a single intermolecular disulfide bond that stabilizes the dimer.
source: BMP4 folds into a cystine knot containing three stereotypical intramolecular disulfide bonds that stabilize ligand monomers and a single intermolecular disulfide bond that stabilizes the dimer (Schwarz, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The addition of an ectopic cysteine residue may lead to aberrant intramolecular or intermolecular disulfide bonds in the BMP4 precursor protein.
source: The addition of an ectopic cysteine residue may lead to aberrant intramolecular or intermolecular disulfide bonds in the precursor protein, as suggested by biochemical analysis of BMP4S91C homodimers expressed in cultured mammalian cells (Tabatabaeifar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Bmp4S91C/E93G compound heterozygotes have a less severe phenotype than Bmp4S91C/S91C mice.
source: This interpretation is consistent with our finding that Bmp4S91C/E93G compound heterozygotes have a less severe phenotype than Bmp4S91C/S91C mice, and with our observation that ectopically expressed BMP4S91D generates significantly higher activity in Xenopus embryos than does BMP4S91C.
evidence: This is supported by phenotypic analysis of the different genotypes.

claim: Ectopically expressed BMP4S91D generates significantly higher activity in Xenopus embryos than does BMP4S91C.
source: This interpretation is consistent with our finding that Bmp4S91C/E93G compound heterozygotes have a less severe phenotype than Bmp4S91C/S91C mice, and with our observation that ectopically expressed BMP4S91D generates significantly higher activity in Xenopus embryos than does BMP4S91C.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Xenopus assays.

claim: Phenotypic and biochemical analysis of Bmp4E93G and Bmp4S91C mice is consistent with a selective loss of BMP4 homodimers rather than BMP4/7 heterodimers.
source: Phenotypic and biochemical analysis of Bmp4E93G and Bmp4S91C mice is consistent with a selective loss of BMP4 homodimers rather than BMP4/7 heterodimers.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phenotypic and biochemical data from the mutant mice.

claim: Mice homozygous for a mutation (Bmp7R-GFlag) that disrupts the formation of functional BMP2/7 and BMP4/7 heterodimers die by E11.5.

evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Mice compound heterozygous for the Bmp7R-GFlag and Bmp4 null alleles die by E11.5.
source: We have previously shown that mice homozygous for a mutation (Bmp7R-GFlag) that disrupts the formation of functional BMP2/7 and BMP4/7 heterodimers, or mice compound heterozygous for the Bmp7R-GFlag and Bmp4 null alleles die by E11.5 (Kim et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag and Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp4−/+ mutants show stereotypical heart defects such as thinner myocardial walls, a common atrium, and a small, malformed OFT relative to wild type littermates.
source: Furthermore, whereas Bmp7R-GFlag/R-GFlag and Bmp7R-GFlag/+;Bmp4−/+ mutants show stereotypical heart defects such as thinner myocardial walls, a common atrium, and a small, malformed OFT relative to wild type littermates (Kim et al., 2019), Bmp4S91C/S91C mutant hearts show grossly normal patterning of atria, ventricles and outflow tract while Bmp4−/E93G mutant hearts show reduced myocardial trabeculation and VSDs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The late lethality and heart defects observed in Bmp4−/E93G mutant mice phenocopy those observed in Ngly1 mutant mice.
source: The late lethality and heart defects observed in Bmp4−/E93G mutant mice phenocopy those observed in Ngly1 mutant mice, which have a selective loss of BMP4 homodimers, but not heterodimers (Fujihira et al., 2017; Galeone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Ngly1 mutant mice have a selective loss of BMP4 homodimers, but not heterodimers.
source: The late lethality and heart defects observed in Bmp4−/E93G mutant mice phenocopy those observed in Ngly1 mutant mice, which have a selective loss of BMP4 homodimers, but not heterodimers (Fujihira et al., 2017; Galeone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Ngly1 and Bmp4−/E93G mutant mice both show VSDs, poorly elaborated myocardial trabeculation and late stage (P0) lethality.
source: Ngly1 and Bmp4−/E93G mutant mice both show VSDs, poorly elaborated myocardial trabeculation and late stage (P0) lethality (Fujihira et al., 2017; Galeone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research and data from the current study.

claim: NGLY1 is a deglycosylase that is required to clear misfolded BMP4 precursor monomers from the ER.
source: NGLY1 is a deglycosylase that is required to clear misfolded BMP4 precursor monomers from the ER.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NGLY1 function.

claim: NGLY1 promotes the formation of properly folded BMP4 homodimers that can be transported out of the ER to be cleaved to generate the functional ligand.
source: This, in turn, promotes the formation of properly folded BMP4 homodimers that can be transported out of the ER to be cleaved to generate the functional ligand (Galeone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The Drosophila ortholog of NGLY1 (Pngl1) is required for formation of functional Dpp homodimers, but not heterodimers.
